To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
postorganization activities can improve the acquisition of knowledge from a knowledge map.

1) postorganization activities that use a graphical knowledge map as an organizational structure improve learning of the information presented in the knowledge map; 2) postorganization activities with a graphical knowledge map that use the knowledge map structure are more effective than activities that use only the knowledge map as a summary aid; and 3) postorganization activities using the knowledge map structure as an aid are more effective than no-cue activities.
postorganization activities can be effective in enhancing recall of superordinate information from knowledge maps.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to improve learning from a knowledge map.
the role that the organization of knowledge plays in the acquisition, retention, and use of information.
the question of whether the postorganization of the material presented on a knowledge map can improve learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the postorganization strategy of studying the map and then organizing it into a summary structure is superior to studying the map and organizing the information without any type of summary structure, as well as superior to studying the knowledge map without organizing the information into any summary structure.
the postorganization strategies that were used by the participants in the 3 groups were not sufficient to enhance the learning of the information that was presented in a knowledge map.
the postorganization strategies of using the knowledge-map format and summarizing the information in a structured manner were effective in enhancing recall of superordinate information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a knowledge-map format and postorganization activities are beneficial to the learning process.
knowledge maps are an effective means of presenting information, but that the use of postorganization strategies can improve the effectiveness of this medium.
the structure of knowledge maps is a useful cue in the acquisition of knowledge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
postorganization activities that are based on the map’s structure are more effective than those that are based on its content.
the structure of a knowledge map can be used to help students recall information presented in a map format.
the use of a graphical post-organization strategy can improve learning outcomes.
